column1: # D RESERVATION LEDGER — a number is SPOKEN FOR here before the charter carries it.
# FOR .claude/workflows/bp-deploy-reliability-charter.md. Enforced by the SAME
# arbiter the PDS charter uses, behind a prefix argument — there is exactly one
# implementation:
#     bash deploy/d-number-arbiter.sh --allocate-d <n> --for <label>   # MINT
#     bash deploy/d-number-arbiter.sh --check-alloc                     # ENFORCE
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-09-16 two PRs in flight the same hour both read
# the charter, both correctly found the highest number defined was D613, and
# both minted D614. #18700 merged and kept it; #18701 rebased and renumbered.
# Neither reader was careless: a document is a lagging record of what has
# LANDED and cannot express what is IN FLIGHT. Two correct readers a minute
# apart get the same answer. Only a claim written down BEFORE the charter edit
# closes that window, and that is what a row here is.
# THE SEED IS 615, DERIVED WITH THE STRICT UNION LENS — bold-lead bullet UNION
# own-line heading, charter_defined_numbers() in scripts/pds-record-parity.sh —
# which reads 633 definitions over 615 distinct numbers, contiguous 1..615.
# A NAIVE `\bD[0-9]+\b` SCAN READS 716 AND IS WRONG: the charter's prose cites
# PDS-D716 (the PDS charter's fence adjudication) six times, and a loose lens
# reads that cross-charter citation as this charter's high-water. That is the
# same trap the PDS ledger warns about with its PDS-D777/PDS-D999 fixtures.
# Numbers at or below the SEED predate the arbiter and are not scored — a
# retroactive reservation would be a claim about history nobody measured.
# number
SEED
